Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m starting with `README.md`, then I’ll apply the required fish-control transfer protocol and inspect both wake-visual views before touching the candidate. I’ll keep all changes inside this Phase 2 workspace and verify that exactly one solver candidate plus both required documentation updates are present.

I’m using two workspace skills: the fish-control shelf because the user explicitly requires its structured transfer protocol, and the wake-visual skill because this policy decision depends on comparing the two prescribed 3D wake views. Any mechanism I borrow will be translated only as a body-frame/state-feedback invariant and documented with a falsification test.

The sampled set appears to contain four copies of the same successful rollout, while the inherited guidance carries the failure history. I’m checking byte identity and the full diagnostics now; if all four are truly identical, I’ll treat this as replicated positive evidence and explicitly note that no sampled failure image exists rather than inventing a visual comparison.

The successful rollout is genuinely replicated: all four candidates, trajectory tables, and combined keyframe sheets are byte-identical, with uniform-direct still-water initialization and capture at `24.6400146T`/`0.748356L`. The top-down row shows self-propelled progress with an alternating reverse-von-Kármán-like wake that bends only in the terminal hook; the oblique row confirms discrete three-dimensional loop structures rather than passive advection. I’m now consulting the shelf because the inherited v38–v40 sequence had three completed non-semantic terminal refinements, which triggers the protocol.

The evidence rules out another terminal gain, threshold, or cross-joint redistribution. I’m narrowing the candidate to a state-feedback phase mechanism: retain the proven residual and route, but make its half-cycle admission depend on the follower’s observed motion as well as the lagged target wave. This tests whether steering is spent only when the posterior traveling bend has actually caught up, without transferring rejected effort to the anterior anchor. I’m replaying the parent trace to bound locality and identify the sign convention before recording the pre-edit hypothesis.

The fixed-trace audit shows why the refinement is testable: v41’s terminal residual is active only from `2.099L` inward, but the posterior joint is already near `−44°`; 97 of 245 active samples occur while that follower is moving inward and 148 while it is moving outward or further loading the same side. I’m recording a bounded, mirror-equivariant posterior-only motion gate now. The anterior v41 phase anchor and every far-route command remain unchanged; the tail receives no extra authority and rejected effort is not moved between joints.

The post-edit replay confirms the intended locality: 238 parent states change, all between `2.099L` and `0.765L`; the anterior command and every command outside `2.10L` are exactly unchanged. The largest posterior difference is `0.191 rad/T²`, far below the `31.416 rad/T²` envelope. On 143 rows, removing outward terminal counter-steer exposes up to `0.164 rad/T²` more of the existing inward brake, so I’m documenting that nuance rather than claiming the total command magnitude can never rise.

The durable guidance now records the strongest reusable result from this generation: four exact v41 replications establish deterministic repeatability of the small phase-allocation gain, but not robustness, because the sample has no distinct failure, reflected pose, perturbed release, or external-wake case. I’m moving to contract/schema checks and the required workspace check-runner; no CFD will be run.

The configured check-runner helper could not start because its fixed `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this account. I’ll still execute all three commands from its TOML exactly as specified. Before that, I’m tightening the gate’s applicability: it will blend back to the proven v41 allocation when the posterior joint is away from its stroke reserve, so centered held-out motion is not needlessly altered.

The first required check exposed a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` lists the same assigned guidance parent twice as “prefill,” so the checker sees two parents. I’m removing that exact duplicate manifest entry, then rerunning the check; this does not alter solver behavior or guidance content.

All three required checks now pass after the duplicate-parent manifest repair: guidance semantics, finite two-joint contract, and solver boundary. The final mechanism probes also confirm the applicability boundary—gate `1.0` at centered stroke, `0.0481` for an outward near-limit follower, and identical even gating under reflection with opposite signed outputs. I’m doing one final artifact/diff audit and then I’ll hand off the single unevaluated candidate.

Implemented exactly one candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl).

It preserves v41’s anterior phase anchor and adds a bounded posterior inward-motion/stroke-pressure gate confined to the terminal `2.10L` region.

Also updated:

- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md) with two-view diagnosis, bookshelf transfer block, hypothesis, and audits.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:219) with the reusable four-replication lesson.
- Removed a duplicate parent marker from `README.md` that initially broke validation.

All three prescribed checks pass: guidance semantics, finite two-joint contract/schema, and solver boundary. The configured check-runner agent model was unavailable, so its exact commands were executed directly. No CFD was run.
